Both forms of the link were proven to work. The raw.githubusercontent.com links were fetched and returned code 200, with byte sizes exactly matching the catalogue. As for the links via the CDN network, they could not be verified from the environment that created this page — since outbound connection to cdn.jsdelivr.net is blocked there — and so they were constructed according to jsDelivr's documented URL format, and the owner tried one of them manually on 2026-09-20. Both were kept: one of them costs this project nothing to serve, and the reader who finds one of them unavailable still has the other.

An ingested copy — not the World Health Organization, and not a live site. This page is generated by {folioAssistant} from its own catalogue of the {iris} repository, modelled by reference: {figures}. The World Health Organization logo was deliberately removed, and the generated covers are not displayed for the same reason, since they carry the logo printed on the publications.
An ingested replicated copy. Created from {catalogue} by {generator}. The design is modelled on {iris}; and every number on this page is read from the catalogue, not copied from a screenshot.

There is no Dublin Core record. The catalogue states this instead of generating descriptive metadata from a PDF file — which is rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill: never infer descriptive metadata from a PDF file when a record exists, and its converse is that an absent record stays absent.

This is the front gate, not the library viewer. The full viewer for library/ is task jbx2, and it is being built separately. This page imitates the IRIS home page and refers onward beyond it, instead of becoming a second answer to the same question.

Three routes to one item, and this is intended. The catalogue knows this item only once; and the bytes are available at the original source at the World Health Organization, and here as a replicated-copy page, and from an edge node in the CDN network — since jsDelivr serves any public repository, so the last route costs this project no hosting. The knowledge graph says what exists and where; as for the CDN network, it says nothing and merely serves it.

Where the held copies actually are — task yl5w. The catalogue records each one of them at uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and all three paths are missing: #477 moved the library/ directory to this instance and left uploads/ in cat-harness/.

Each row offers three routes to the same item: the source in IRIS at the original source at the World Health Organization, and the local replicated copy page belonging to this repository, and the resource itself — downloadable from the repository, and separately from an edge node in the CDN network.

Every row below is active. A row does not appear in grey when this repository does not hold it; rather {referenced} is written in it, which is the actual state and the whole purpose of a catalogue modelled by reference. As for {materialized}, it means that the bytes are present here.

The download links above point to where the bytes are actually, and therefore they work. The error, rather, is in the catalogue's claim, and check:catalogue does not verify localPath at all — it verifies metadataRef and libraryId, and reports a clean run on three materialized claims that point to nothing.

The interface is displayed in the language: {language}. As for the titles of publications, their authors, their abstracts and the other catalogue records, they are displayed as the World Health Organization published them.

The main objective of the Institutional Repository for Information Sharing (IRIS) is to provide free digital access to the scientific and technical publications of the World Health Organization, including the contributions of its country offices, its regional offices and its headquarters. In addition, IRIS includes the mandates set by the Organization's governing bodies in cooperation with its Member States.
